title: Ten copies of a megabyte unit sort 27 times slower than normal DNA of the same size
body:
`create --dna --write-lcp` on a 10 MiB record made of ten copies of one 1 MiB unit, with one random base between copies, takes 6.8 s on 8 threads at 069d033. The normal 10 MiB fixture takes 0.25 s. The time is quadratic in the size: 1.55 s at 5 MiB, 6.8 s at 10 MiB, 43.6 s at 25 MiB.

The copy count decides it, at a fixed 10 MiB:

| copies | unit | head | all mitigations off |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 5 MiB | 0.27 s | 30.4 s |
| 10 | 1 MiB | 6.8 s | 52.7 s |
| 100 | 100 KiB | 1.7 s | 11.9 s |

With two copies the LCP cache in `libsufr/src/lcp.rs` and the merge's skip carry the whole cost, 113 times. With ten copies they buy 7.8 times and head is still 27 times the normal fixture. The cache keys an entry by the distance between the two suffixes and keeps one interval per slot; nine distances fit in 65,536 slots, so slot collisions are not the reason. `suffix_lcp` caches only an LCP that stopped short of `len`, and in the merge `len` is `context - m`, so a compare capped by `context` leaves nothing in the cache. Whether that is what happens with ten copies is not checked.

The fixtures are `benchmarks/runs/long-repeats-10.fa` and the two-copy and hundred-copy variants written by `tmp-claude/2026-11-03-benchmarks/variants.py`. The patched builds are the worktrees under the same directory.
